title: Median Hawker Stall Rentals in Last Two Years and Proposed Balloting Model Based on Cost Recovery for Such Stalls
what_it_is: Median Hawker Stall Rentals in Last Two Years and Proposed Balloting Model Based on Cost Recovery for Such Stalls

sections.label: Cooked food stall tender prices
sections.summary: About one in five cooked food stalls got tender prices at or below $500 a month in 2023, with median prices of about $2,000 in 2022 and $1,800 in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: About one in five cooked food stalls was awarded tender prices at or below $500 a month in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The median successful tender price for cooked food stalls across hawker centres was about $2,000 in 2022 and $1,800 in 2023.

sections.label: Hawkers hiring LTVP stall assistants
sections.summary: Policy will be relaxed to allow hawkers to hire LTVP or LTVP+ holders with LOCs or Pre-approved LOCs as stall assistants.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To provide additional support to stallholders at hawker centres managed by NEA or NEA-appointed operators, we will further relax our policy to allow hawkers to hire LTVP or LTVP+ holders with LOCs or Pre-approved LOCs to work as their stall assistants.

sections.label: More granular NEA website information
sections.summary: More granular information will be put on the NEA website so potential bidders are more cognisant of price points they compete against.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: What we can do, in response to his second suggestion of putting some form of alert to help bidders to be more considered in their prices when it comes to bidding for a rental stall, is to put out a bit more granular information on the NEA website, so that a potential bidder would be more cognisant of the kind of price points that he is competing against, fellow stall owners in the same hawker centre.

sections.label: Bidding process and manpower support
sections.summary: More NEA website information on market rent will be provided, bidding process adjustments considered, and Work Permit liberalisation not done now, with productivity grants enhanced.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: One thing which I said earlier is about putting more information on the NEA website, so that when the bidder comes in, he is aware of what his fellow stallholders are actually paying as market rent.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We will take some of these considerations that the Member has raised and see how best we can, maybe, make adjustments even to the bidding process, so that these excessive high bids will be something that is lesser than what it is today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The first question is: when he said one in five hawker stalls have rental below $500, does that statistic include non-cooked food stalls?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Because, currently, as far as we know, there is a scheme called the mini-restaurant licence scheme, whereby some hawkers at the coffee shops and food courts are allowed to employ Work Permit holders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And for the second question on whether we were going to liberalise it to, in general, Work Permit holders, the answer is, not at this moment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The numbers today are very small to begin with.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And while we want to help solve their manpower challenges in the immediate term, the more sustainable way forward is to continue to help them to adopt more resilient and more productive methods, which is why we enhanced the Productive Hawker Centre Grant to do things at a centralised level, to make the hawker centre more productive through things like centralised dishwashing, for example.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We will also continue to enhance the Hawkers Productivity Grant, where the hawkers themselves can take on more productive methods of preparing their food.
